definition_zh: 娶；嫁；与……结婚；使结合、使交融（be wedded to）
definition_en: to marry someone, or to join two things closely together
core_image: 两只手在众人面前交握，从此被一句话绑在一起
scene: 小教堂里只有十几个人，新娘的父亲把她的手交到新郎手里。 They were wed in a small church on a rainy April morning.
sceneCN: 这里 wed 是「与……结婚」（第 1 个义项：正式结为夫妻）；句意为他们在四月一个下雨的早晨于小教堂成婚。两只在众人面前交握的手，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：娶、嫁；使成婚；使紧密结合

collocations.zh: 把理论与实践结合起来

derivatives.zh: 由过去分词转形容词，义为「已婚的；结合的」
复合词，义为「婚姻状态」，多用于 born out of wedlock
与婚礼相关的同义词根词，义为「新娘的」

senses.title: To marry
senses.definition: to marry someone, used especially in formal, literary or journalistic writing
senses.definitionCN: 与某人结婚，多用于正式、文学或新闻报道语体
senses.example: The couple were wed last spring in the village church.
senses.exampleCN: 这对新人去年春天在村里的教堂成婚。
senses.why: Old English weddian meant to pledge or to give as a surety; marriage is the chief pledge people make.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 weddian 意为「许诺、作保」，婚姻便是人最主要的一种许诺。

senses.title: To be joined closely
senses.titleCN: 紧密结合：两样东西被牢牢连在一起
senses.definition: of two things, to be joined or combined closely
senses.definitionCN: 指两样事物被紧密连接或结合
senses.example: The old songs wed words to a rhythm that everyone could walk to.
senses.exampleCN: 那些老歌把词与人人能踏上的节奏连在一起。
senses.why: The pledge image works for things too: two sides are bound by a promise-like union.
senses.whyCN: 许诺的意象也适用于事物：两边由一种类似誓约的结合绑在一起。

senses.title: To be devoted to
senses.titleCN: 执着于：一心只守着某观念
senses.definition: in the phrase be wedded to, to be firmly attached to an idea or method and unwilling to change
senses.definitionCN: 用于 be wedded to，指死死守持某种观念或方法而不肯改变
senses.example: The department is wedded to a system that has not worked for years.
senses.exampleCN: 这个部门死守着一套多年不见效的制度。
senses.why: A vow was meant to be unbreakable, and that stubbornness passes over to opinions.
senses.whyCN: 誓言本意是不可违背的，这种固执便转移到了看法上。

senses.title: Newly married
senses.definition: used adjectivally in phrases such as newly wed and wedded couple
senses.definitionCN: 以形容词形式用于 newly wed、wedded couple 等短语
senses.example: The newly wed pair left for the coast that same evening.
senses.exampleCN: 新婚夫妇当晚就去了海边。
senses.why: The participle freezes the event into a state, so the marriage becomes a lasting description.
senses.whyCN: 分词把事件凝固成状态，于是这场婚成了持续的描摹。

senses.title: In journalistic headlines
senses.definition: a short, formal substitute for marry, common in newspapers and announcements
senses.definitionCN: 作为 marry 的简短正式替代词，常见于报纸与公告
senses.example: She wed the lead singer in 1998, a year after the album.
senses.exampleCN: 她在 1998 年与主唱成婚，那是在那张专辑一年之后。
senses.why: Brevity suits headlines, and the word carries just the right formal weight.
senses.whyCN: 标题求短，而这个词恰有合适的正式分量。

intro.en: Wed goes back to an Old English verb for pledging, and marriage was its greatest pledge.
intro.cn: wed 可追溯到古英语表示「许诺」的动词，而婚姻是其中最重的一种许诺。

items.en: Weddian meant 'to pledge, to promise, to give surety', and also 'to marry'.
items.cn: weddian 意为「许诺、担保」，也有「结婚」之义。

items.en: The noun wedd meant a pledge or a surety, the thing given so that a promise would hold.
items.cn: 名词 wedd 意为「誓约、担保」，即为了许诺兑现而交付的东西。

items.en: German Wette 'a bet' and Gothic wadi 'pledge' belong to the same old word group.
items.cn: 德语 Wette「赌注」与哥特语 wadi「抵押」同属这一古老词群。

items.en: Wedded became the usual past form, and wedding came to mean the ceremony itself.
items.cn: wedded 成为常规过去式，wedding 则转指婚礼本身。

items.en: The verb narrowed to formal use, while the metaphor of wedded to an idea kept its force.
items.cn: 这个动词收窄为正式用法，而 wedded to 某观念的比喻仍保有力量。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the pledge family; the near-meaning group gathers marriage verbs of different weight.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「许诺」词族的词；近义组收分量不同的婚姻动词。

entries.definition: The ceremony of marriage and the party that follows.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「婚礼」及随之的喜宴。

entries.definition: Married, or firmly attached to something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「已婚的」，或「紧密结合的」。

entries.definition: The married state; the -lock element belonged to the old noun pledge.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「婚姻状态」，其中 -lock 部分出自古老的「誓约」义。

entries.definition: Pay for work; an old relative of pledge and bet.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「工资」，与「抵押、许诺」一义有古老亲缘。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for becoming husband or wife.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「结婚」，是最日常的说法。

entries.definition: To marry, often in old texts; also to support a cause.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「娶、嫁」，多见于旧文本，也指拥护某个主张。

entries.definition: To join into one; the plain word for the figurative sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「联合」，是比喻义上的朴素说法。

entries.definition: To end a marriage legally; the opposite act.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「离婚」，是相反的动作。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English wedd and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语 wedd，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: wed comes from a word for pledge: a marriage is a promise made public.
normal.cn: wed 出自表示「誓约」的词：婚姻就是一个公开的许诺。

normal.en: Wedding, wedded, wedlock all keep the old vow inside them.
normal.cn: wedding、wedded、wedlock 都把古老的誓约留在里面。

normal.en: Be wedded to an idea means married to it, for better or worse.
normal.cn: be wedded to 某观念意为与它成了婚，无论是好是糟。

normal.en: Newly wed is the headline phrase; the prize is the same as marry.
normal.cn: newly wed 是标题用语，意思与 marry 相同。

normal.en: Past tense wedded is more common than the short wed.
normal.cn: 过去式 wedded 比简短的 wed 更常见。

abstract.en: Picture two hands clasped in front of witnesses: the word is a binding, not just a feeling.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手在众人面前交握：这个词是一种约束，而不只是感情。

abstract.en: Anything can be wedded if it is joined by a promise: words to rhythm, theory to practice.
abstract.cn: 只要有约定相连，任何两样东西都能被 wed：词与节奏、理论与实践。

abstract.en: The stubbornness of wedded to is the stubbornness of a vow no one wants to break.
abstract.cn: wedded to 的固执，正是一个谁都不愿违背的誓言的固执。

examples.en: They were wed after ten years of living in different cities.
examples.cn: 在分居两城十年之后，他们结婚了。

examples.en: The design weds old brick to new glass.
examples.cn: 这一设计把老砖与新玻璃结合在一起。

examples.en: He has been wedded to the same routine for decades.
examples.cn: 几十年来他一直执着于同一套常规。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「wed 就是喂（we）到（d）」——一路喂到婚礼上：结婚

root: 古英语 weddian「许诺、担保、婚配」，名词 wedd「誓约、抵押」，与德语 Wette、哥特语 wadi 同源；派生词有 wedding、wedded、wedlock。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of wed grow out of one pledge: marriage, the joining of things, stubborn devotion, the state of being newly married, and the formal word in headlines.
sensesIntro.cn: wed 的五个义项都生自同一个誓约：婚姻、事务的结合、固执的守持、新婚的状态，以及新闻标题里的正式用词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands clasped before witnesses, bound from then on by one word.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手在众人面前交握，从此被一句话绑在一起。

branches.en: MARRIAGE LINE: the vow performed, then the state it leaves.
branches.cn: 婚姻线：誓约的践行，以及它留下的状态。

branches.en: JOINING LINE: anything can be bound as if by a promise.
branches.cn: 结合线：任何东西都能像被许诺般绑在一起。

branches.en: STUBBORN LINE: a vow nobody wants to break becomes a habit of mind.
branches.cn: 固执线：无人愿破的誓约变成了思维习惯。

branches.en: STYLE LINE: a short formal verb for newspapers.
branches.cn: 语体线：报纸偏爱的简短正式动词。

branches.en: CONTRAST: marry is everyday, wed is formal and brief.
branches.cn: 对照线：marry 日常，wed 正式而简短。

intro.en: Wed is a native verb from the pledge word; its relatives are all forms of the same vow.
intro.cn: wed 是出自「誓约」一词的本族动词；它的亲属都是同一个誓约的不同形式。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved here; the related native forms are listed instead.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不涉及拉丁语成分，只列出相关的本族词形式。

items.example: It is the noun behind the verb.

definition_en: a large organisation such as a university or hospital, or an established custom
core_image: 石阶、石柱和一扇旧木门，门上的铜牌刻着机构的名字
scene: 冬天傍晚，医院门口的灯已经亮起，排队的队伍沿石阶往下。 The hospital is the oldest institution in the town.
sceneCN: 这里 institution 是「机构」（第 1 个义项：大学、医院等大型组织），句意是这家医院是镇上最古老的机构。画面里能看到的物件：石阶、石柱、铜牌、灯。

pos.zh: 名词：机构；制度；由来已久的做法

derivatives.zh: 本词所对应的动词与名词，义为「设立；研究所」
由本词加 -al 构成，义为「机构的；制度性的」
由 institutional 加 -ize 构成，义为「制度化」
由 institutionalize 加 -d 构成，义为「已制度化的」

senses.title: An organisation
senses.definition: a large organisation set up for a public or professional purpose, such as a bank or a university
senses.definitionCN: 为公共或专业目的建立的大型组织，如银行或大学
senses.example: The museum is a public institution and entrance is free.
senses.exampleCN: 这家博物馆是公共机构，免费入场。
senses.why: Latin instituere "to set up" gives the result noun: something set up and standing on its own.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 instituere「设立」给出结果名词：被设立起来、独立存在的东西。

senses.title: An established custom
senses.titleCN: 由来已久的习俗与制度
senses.definition: a custom or practice that a society has long accepted and rarely questions
senses.definitionCN: 一个社会长期接受、很少质疑的习俗或做法
senses.example: The Sunday dinner is an institution in that family.
senses.exampleCN: 星期日聚餐在那个家庭里是雷打不动的惯例。
senses.why: A practice set up long ago and never taken down is felt as a thing standing there.
senses.whyCN: 很久以前设立、从未撤下的做法，会被感受为一件一直立在那里的事物。

senses.title: A place for care
senses.definition: a building where people are cared for over long periods, often used in older writing
senses.definitionCN: 长期照料人的场所，旧文常用此说法
senses.example: The old building was once an institution for orphaned children.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋旧楼曾是收容孤儿的机构。
senses.why: Buildings set up to keep and care for people took the general word for a set-up place.
senses.whyCN: 为收容和照料人而设立的场所沿用了「设立之处的通称」。

intro.en: Institution is the Latin noun of result from instituere "to set up", literally "something that has been set up".
intro.cn: institution 是拉丁语 instituere「设立」的结果名词，字面是「被设立起来的东西」。

items.en: Statuere "to make stand" and instituere "to set up" are both classical.
items.cn: statuere「使站立」与 instituere「设立」都是古典拉丁语词汇。

items.en: The noun institutio named the act of setting up or of teaching.
items.cn: 名词 institutio 指设立的行为或教导。

items.en: Old French institution passed into Middle English with both meanings.
items.cn: 古法语 institution 连同两层含义进入中古英语。

items.en: The eighteenth and nineteenth centuries made it the general word for social bodies.
items.cn: 十八、十九世纪它成为社会组织的通称。

items.en: Modern sociology uses it for customs and norms as well as buildings.
items.cn: 现代社会学用它兼指建筑与习俗规范。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -stitut- stem; the near-meaning group holds other words for organisations and customs.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -stitut- 词干；近义组收其他表示「组织」与「习俗」的词。

entries.definition: A research body, or the verb meaning to set one up.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「研究所」，动词义为「设立」。

entries.definition: The framework of rules that constitutes a state.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「宪法」，构成国家的规则框架。

entries.definition: The act of putting one thing in place of another.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「替换」。

entries.definition: Any structured group, without the sense of long establishment.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「组织」，不强调历史久远。

entries.definition: A usual practice, close to the second sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「习俗」，与第 2 义近义。

entries.definition: A group with a formal purpose, a bare synonym in formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「团体」，正式文体中可同义替换。

normalIntro.en: These hooks link the word to its verb and to the buildings and customs it names.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把本词与它的动词以及它所命名的建筑、习俗联系起来。

normal.en: institute plus -ion: something set up and now standing.
normal.cn: institute 加 -ion：设立起来、如今站立的东西。

normal.en: Banks, hospitals and schools are all institutions.
normal.cn: 银行、医院、学校都是 institution。

normal.en: Institutional reform changes the rules, not the walls.
normal.cn: institutional reform 改的是规则，不是墙。

normal.en: A weekly dinner can be an institution too.
normal.cn: 每周一次的家庭聚餐也可以是一种惯例。

normal.en: Institutionalized people have lived long inside such places.
normal.cn: institutionalized 形容人长期生活在机构之中。

abstract.en: Institutions are habits with stone walls around them.
abstract.cn: 制度是围上了石墙的习惯。

abstract.en: A phrase becomes an institution once nobody remembers inventing it.
abstract.cn: 当一个说法没人记得是谁发明的，它就成了惯例。

abstract.en: Institutions are slow to change and slow to fall.
abstract.cn: 机构改变得慢，崩塌也慢。

examples.en: The bank is a respected financial institution.
examples.cn: 这家银行是受人尊敬的金融机构。

examples.en: Marriage is a social institution that varies by culture.
examples.cn: 婚姻是一种因文化而异的社会制度。

examples.en: They campaigned for institutional reform.
examples.cn: 他们为制度改革而奔走。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬是提土伸」——硬是提土伸出手，把机构搭起来

root: 拉丁语 statuere「使站立」→ instituere「设立」→ 名词 institutio「设立；教导」→ 古法语 institution → 中古英语。与 institute、constitute、substitute 同族，现代社会学用其指制度与习俗。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a formal organisation, a long-accepted custom, and an older word for a care home.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：正式组织、长期被接受的习俗，以及旧时指照料机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: stone steps, pillars and an old wooden door with a brass nameplate.
core.cn: 核心意象：石阶、石柱与刻着名字的旧木门。

branches.en: THE DOORPLATE: a bank, a school, a museum.
branches.cn: 门牌这条线：银行、学校、博物馆。

branches.en: THE CALENDAR: a habit repeated until it is a rule.
branches.cn: 日历这条线：重复成规则的习俗。

branches.en: THE WARD: a place where people are cared for over years.
branches.cn: 病房这条线：长期照料人的场所。

branches.en: THE LINK: buildings and customs share the idea of an accepted arrangement.
branches.cn: 连接线：建筑与习俗共享「被接受的安排」这一观念。

branches.en: THE TONE: the care sense today sounds old or institutional.
branches.cn: 语气线：照料义如今显得陈旧或冷硬。

intro.en: Institution is in- plus the Latin stem statu- "set standing", with the noun ending -io.
intro.cn: institution 是 in- 加拉丁词干 statu-「使站立」，再加名词词尾 -io。

latinIntro.en: Latin instituere and institutio are both recorded, so this layer is fully attested.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 instituere 与 institutio 均有记载，这一层完全有据。

items.example: The result sense dominates in English.
Institutional describes what belongs to institutions.
items.exampleCN: institutional 描述属于机构的事物。

items.example: Institutionalize makes something part of an institution.
items.exampleCN: institutionalize 指使之成为机构的一部分。

items.example: The shorter verb in the same family.

items.meaning: the setting up of a state

items.example: A native synonym of the first sense.
items.exampleCN: 第一义的本族语近义词。

definition_en: showing strong excitement and interest
core_image: 眼睛里发亮，身体前倾，抢着把喜欢的事说给别人听
scene: 新来的志愿者一进门就热情地介绍起周末的活动安排。 The new volunteer was enthusiastic about the weekend programme from the moment she arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 enthusiastic 是「热情的」（第 1 个义项：表现出强烈兴趣）；句意：新志愿者一进门就对周末的活动安排充满热情。

senses.title: Showing strong eager interest
senses.definition: showing a lot of excitement and interest in something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物表现出大量兴奋与兴趣
senses.example: The children were enthusiastic about the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们对这次旅行充满热情。
senses.why: The -ic adjective turns the inner fire of enthusiasm into a visible quality.
senses.whyCN: -ic 形容词把 enthusiasm 的内心之火变成看得见的品质。

senses.title: Eager to take part
senses.definition: very willing to join an activity or help
senses.definitionCN: 非常愿意参加活动或提供帮助
senses.example: The volunteers were enthusiastic about starting work at once.
senses.exampleCN: 志愿者们恨不得马上开始工作。
senses.why: Eagerness to act is enthusiasm directed at doing something.
senses.whyCN: 急于行动，就是指向做事的热情。

senses.title: Expressing warm approval
senses.definition: showing strong and warm support for a plan or idea
senses.definitionCN: 对计划或想法表现出强烈而热烈的支持
senses.example: The plan won enthusiastic support from the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 这项计划赢得了全队的热烈支持。
senses.why: Approval becomes enthusiastic when it is expressed with the same heat as interest.
senses.whyCN: 当赞同以与兴趣同样的热度表达出来，就成了「热烈赞同」。

intro.en: Enthusiastic is enthusiasm with the adjective ending -ic, from Greek entheos, having a god within.
intro.cn: enthusiastic 是 enthusiasm 加形容词词尾 -ic，源于希腊语 entheos（心中有神）。

items.en: Theos means god, and entheos means inspired by a god.
items.cn: theos 意为神，entheos 意为受神启发的。

items.en: Enthousiasmos means divine possession or inspired fervor.
items.cn: enthousiasmos 意为神灵附体或受神启的热忱。

items.en: Enthusiasmus brings the noun into Latin learning.
items.cn: enthusiasmus 把这个名词带入拉丁学术。

items.en: Enthusiasm enters English with its religious intensity.
items.cn: 到 17 世纪，enthusiasm 带着宗教强度进入英语。

items.en: The ending -ic forms enthusiastic as a describing word.
items.cn: 到 18 世纪，词尾 -ic 构成形容词 enthusiastic。

items.en: Enthusiastic now describes visible eagerness in any field.
items.cn: 现代英语中，enthusiastic 描述任何领域中看得见的热情。

note.en: Enthusiastic is the -ic adjective of enthusiasm, and it sits near its family and near words for eager and keen.
note.cn: enthusiastic 是 enthusiasm 的 -ic 形容词，与自身词族以及表示渴望和热切的词相邻。

entries.definition: strong excited interest
entries.definitionCN: 热情；热忱

entries.definition: a person who is very interested
entries.definitionCN: 热衷者

entries.definition: in an eager way
entries.definitionCN: 热情地

entries.definition: wanting to do something very much
entries.definitionCN: 渴望的

entries.definition: very interested and enthusiastic
entries.definitionCN: 热切的；热衷的

entries.definition: having very strong feelings
entries.definitionCN: 充满激情的

normalIntro.en: Enthusiastic is enthusiasm turned into an adjective with -ic.
normalIntro.cn: enthusiastic 是 enthusiasm 加 -ic 变成的形容词。

normal.en: Drop -ism and add -ic: the noun becomes the describing word.
normal.cn: 去掉 -ism 加上 -ic，名词就变成形容词。

normal.en: Enthusiastic about is the most common pattern.
normal.cn: enthusiastic about 是最常见的搭配。

normal.en: An enthusiastic response is louder than a polite one.
normal.cn: enthusiastic response 比礼貌性的回应更热烈。

normal.en: The adverb enthusiastically adds -ally to the adjective.
normal.cn: 副词 enthusiastically 在形容词后加 -ally。

normal.en: Compare keen: keen is quieter and more common in British English.
normal.cn: 对比 keen：keen 更含蓄，在英式英语中更常见。

abstract.en: Picture hands raised before the question is finished.
abstract.cn: 想象问题还没问完，手已经举起来。

abstract.en: Imagine a door thrown open for a guest.
abstract.cn: 想象门被猛地拉开迎接客人。

abstract.en: Think of a face lit by a screen at midnight.
abstract.cn: 想象午夜时分被屏幕照亮的一张脸。

examples.en: The children were enthusiastic about the trip.
examples.cn: 孩子们对这次旅行充满热情。

examples.en: She gave an enthusiastic welcome to the guests.
examples.cn: 她热情地欢迎客人。

examples.en: His enthusiastic support helped the plan succeed.
examples.cn: 他的热情支持帮助计划取得成功。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「enthusiasm + tic」——热情像小动作一样藏不住，一阵一阵往外冒；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 theos（神）→ entheos（心中有神的）→ enthousiasmos（受神启的激情）→ 拉丁语 enthusiasmus → 英语 enthusiasm ＋ -ic → enthusiastic。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective describes the outer signs of the inner fire: bright interest, readiness to act, and warm approval.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个形容词描述内心之火的外在迹象：明亮的兴趣、随时行动的意愿，以及热烈的赞同。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit face leaning forward, eager to speak or act.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张发亮的脸向前倾，急着说话或行动。

branches.en: Visible interest is the basic adjective sense.
branches.cn: 看得见的兴趣，是形容词的基本义项。

branches.en: Readiness to act turns interest into participation.
branches.cn: 随时行动的意愿把兴趣变成参与。

branches.en: Warm approval directs the same energy at a plan.
branches.cn: 热烈赞同把同样的能量指向一项计划。

branches.en: An interested person usually wants to join in.
branches.cn: 有兴趣的人通常想参与。

branches.en: Eager helpers often give loud support.
branches.cn: 热心的帮手常常给出响亮的支持。

intro.en: Enthusiastic is enthusiasm reshaped with the adjective ending -ic.
intro.cn: enthusiastic 是 enthusiasm 加上形容词词尾 -ic 构成的。

latinIntro.en: Greek theos, god, lies behind the whole family, and the -ic ending is English.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 theos（神）是整个词族的根源，-ic 词尾则来自英语。

items.exampleCN: en- 出现在 entheos 开头。

items.example: Theos is the heart of the family.
items.exampleCN: theos 是这个词族的核心。

items.example: Entheos supplies the image of inner fire.
items.exampleCN: entheos 提供内心之火的画面。

items.example: Enthousiasmos is the Greek noun source.
items.exampleCN: enthousiasmos 是希腊语名词来源。

items.example: Enthusiastic describes a person or response.

definition_zh: 心理学；心理；心理状态；心理战；洞察人心的策略
definition_en: the study of the soul and then of the mind, and by extension the mental life of a person or group and the practical art of reading it
core_image: 一个人俯身倾听自己胸腔里的呼吸，试图从那口看不见的气息里读出心灵的模样
scene: 决赛前的更衣室里，灯很亮，气氛绷得很紧，教练俯下身对球员低声说话。 A coach leans toward a nervous player and says: I am not a therapist, but a little psychology won't hurt before a final.
sceneCN: 这里 psychology 是「心理/洞察人心的策略」（第 5 个义项，兼含第 2 个义项）；句意：我不是心理医生，但用一点心理学不会有害——我知道你在决赛前心里怎么想。画面里有场边、毛巾和低着头的球员。

pos.zh: 心理学；心理；心理状态；心理战术

derivatives.zh: 作心理学解释；用心理分析
心理主义（用心理事实解释一切的倾向）

senses.title: The science of the mind
senses.titleCN: 心理学：研究心灵的那门科学
senses.definition: the scientific study of the mind and behavior
senses.definitionCN: 对心理与行为的科学研究
senses.example: She studied psychology to understand how memory works.
senses.exampleCN: 她学习心理学，以理解记忆如何运作。
senses.why: The word is recorded in the 1650s as 'the study of the soul', from Modern Latin psychologia, probably coined in Germany in the mid-16c. By 1748 it meant the science of mental phenomena; by the early 1890s, a behavioral science.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在 17 世纪 50 年代记录为“对灵魂的研究”，来自新拉丁语 psychologia，很可能是 16 世纪中在德国造出的。到 1748 年它指“心理现象的科学”，到 19 世纪 90 年代初成为行为科学。

senses.title: The mind of a person: mental makeup
senses.titleCN: 心理、心理状态：一个人心里的那套构造
senses.definition: the mental and emotional makeup of a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体的心理与情感构成
senses.example: The psychology of the crowd turned angry within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 人群的心理在几分钟内变得愤怒。
senses.why: The name of the discipline slid over to its object. If psychology is the study of the mind, 'the psychology of X' is the mind of X — the thing studied rather than the study.
senses.whyCN: 学科名滑向了它的研究对象。如果 psychology 是研究心灵的学问，那么“X 的 psychology”就是 X 的心灵——是研究对象，而不是研究本身。

senses.title: Weapons of the mind: psychological warfare
senses.titleCN: 心理战：不动枪炮，先动人心
senses.definition: the use of propaganda, threats, or staged information to weaken an enemy's morale
senses.definitionCN: 利用宣传、威胁或安排好的信息削弱敌方士气
senses.example: The leaflets were pure psychology: they made the enemy doubt itself.
senses.exampleCN: 那些传单纯粹是心理战：它们让敌人开始怀疑自己。
senses.why: Psychological warfare is recorded in the early 20c.; in compounds and headlines the adjective is clipped, so psychology alone can name the campaign that attacks morale rather than bodies.
senses.whyCN: psychological warfare 记录于 20 世纪初；在复合词和标题里形容词常被省略，于是 psychology 本身就能指那场攻击士气而非身体的行动。

senses.title: A school of thought: one system among many
senses.titleCN: 心理学体系、学派：一家之言
senses.definition: a particular system or school of psychological theory
senses.definitionCN: 某一特定的心理学理论体系或学派
senses.example: Freudian psychology dominated the clinic for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 弗洛伊德心理学在诊所里主导了数十年。
senses.why: -logia means 'study of', but a named body of doctrine also takes the name: Jungian psychology, cognitive psychology. The discipline splits into psychologies, each with its own mind-model.
senses.whyCN: -logia 意为“对……的研究”，但一套有名字的学说也沿用这个名称：荣格心理学、认知心理学。学科分裂成多种 psychology，每一种都有自己的心灵模型。

senses.title: Reading people: practical psychology
senses.titleCN: 洞察人心：能当场用的那点心理学
senses.definition: a shrewd practical understanding of how people think, used to persuade or calm them
senses.definitionCN: 对他人如何思考的敏锐实际理解，用来说服或安抚他人
senses.example: The coach used a little psychology to settle the team before the final.
senses.exampleCN: 教练用了点心理策略，让球队在决赛前平静下来。
senses.why: When theory is applied in the moment, 'psychology' becomes a skill rather than a science: knowing which word will move a person. The abstract noun turns into a countable trick.
senses.whyCN: 当理论被当场应用时，psychology 就成了技能而非科学：知道哪个词能打动一个人。这个抽象名词于是变成了可数的小手段。

senses.title: The empirical science of behavior
senses.titleCN: 行为科学：从实验里长出的那门学问
senses.definition: the modern empirical science of behavior, especially since the 1890s
senses.definitionCN: 现代的经验性行为科学，尤指 19 世纪 90 年代以来
senses.example: Modern psychology relies on controlled experiments and statistics.
senses.exampleCN: 现代心理学依赖受控实验和统计。
senses.why: The behavioral-sciences sense is dated to the early 1890s. Laboratories replaced the armchair: the soul was no longer the object — measurable behavior was.
senses.whyCN: 行为科学义可追溯到 19 世纪 90 年代初。实验室取代了扶手椅：研究对象不再是灵魂，而是可测量的行为。

senses.title: The old study of the soul
senses.titleCN: 灵魂学：这个词最初的意思
senses.definition: the original 1650s sense: the study of the soul or spirit
senses.definitionCN: 17 世纪 50 年代的本义：对灵魂或精神的研究
senses.example: Early psychology was closer to theology than to statistics.
senses.exampleCN: 早期心理学更接近神学，而不是统计学。
senses.why: Greek psykhē meant 'breath, spirit, soul', and -logia 'study of'. Before the mind was measured, it was the breath-like soul that the word set out to study.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 psykhē 意为“呼吸、精神、灵魂”，-logia 意为“研究”。在心智被测量之前，这个词要研究的是那口气息般的灵魂。

senses.title: The mind of a group: consumer and social psychology
senses.titleCN: 群体心理：一群人共享的那颗心
senses.definition: the mental processes of a group, market, or public considered as a subject of study
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个研究对象的群体、市场或公众的心理过程
senses.example: The psychology of consumers shapes every advertising campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 消费者的心理塑造着每一场广告活动。
senses.why: 'The psychology of X' extends the discipline to any collective mind. Advertising, politics and sport all borrow the laboratory's name for the crowd's inner life.
senses.whyCN: “X 的 psychology”把学科扩展到任何集体心智。广告、政治和体育都借实验室的名字，来指人群的内心生活。

senses.title: Inner life in a story
senses.titleCN: 人物心理：小说里被写出来的内心
senses.definition: the inner mental life of a character or work as revealed in art and literature
senses.definitionCN: 艺术与文学中所揭示的人物或作品的内心生活
senses.example: The novel's psychology is revealed through small gestures, not speeches.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说的心理是通过细小动作而非言谈揭示的。
senses.why: Critics borrowed the discipline's name for what a text shows of the mind. The psychology of a character is the mind the writer has built, studied as if from outside.
senses.whyCN: 评论家借用了学科名，指文本所展示的心灵。人物的 psychology 就是作者建造的那颗心，像从外部一样被研究。

intro.en: Psychology starts as the study of the soul, not the brain. Greek psykhē 'breath, spirit' plus -logia 'study of' produced a Modern Latin coinage of the 16c.; English took it in the 1650s, and the object shifted from soul to mind to measurable behavior.
intro.cn: psychology 起初研究的是灵魂，不是大脑。希腊语 psykhē“呼吸、精神”加 -logia“对……的研究”造出一个 16 世纪的新拉丁语词；英语在 17 世纪 50 年代借入，研究对象从灵魂转到心智，再转到可测量的行为。

items.en: Psykhē meant 'breath, spirit, soul, life', probably akin to psykhein 'to blow, breathe'. The deeper PIE *bhes- 'to blow' is a reconstruction with no written record, so that layer is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: psykhē 意为“呼吸、精神、灵魂、生命”，可能与 psykhein“吹、呼吸”同源。更深的印欧语 *bhes-“吹”是没有书面记录的重构，因此该层标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: -Logia 'study of' comes from logos 'word, reason, account'. A psychology is literally an account of the soul.
items.cn: -logia“对……的研究”来自 logos“言词、理性、论述”。一门 psychology 字面上就是“关于灵魂的论述”。

items.en: Psychologia was probably coined in Germany in the mid-16c., attributed to Melanchthon. It joined the Latinized Greek psykhē to -logia.
items.cn: psychologia 很可能是 16 世纪中在德国造出的，常归于梅兰希顿。它把拉丁化的希腊语 psykhē 与 -logia 结合。

items.en: The word enters English as 'the study of the soul'. The soul, not behavior, is the first object of the new discipline.
items.cn: 这个词进入英语时意为“对灵魂的研究”。新学科最初的对象是灵魂，而不是行为。

items.en: The meaning 'science or study of the phenomena of the mind' is attested by 1748, in reference to Christian Wolff's Psychologia empirica (1732).
items.cn: “研究心理现象的科学”这一义项于 1748 年出现，指的是克里斯蒂安·沃尔夫的《经验心理学》（1732）。

items.en: The modern behavioral-sciences sense dates from the early 1890s, when laboratories and statistics redefined what counted as the mind's evidence.
items.cn: 现代行为科学义可追溯到 19 世纪 90 年代初，那时实验室与统计重新定义了什么才算心灵的证据。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the psych- or -ology shape but belongs to different roots; the meaning group shares the study or the mind itself.
note.cn: 形近组共享 psych- 或 -ology 的外形，但属于不同词根；近义组共享“研究”或“心灵本身”。

entries.definition: the branch of medicine that treats mental illness. It shares psych- but ends in 'healing', not 'study'.
entries.definitionCN: 治疗精神疾病的医学分支。它共享 psych-，但词尾是“治疗”而非“研究”。

entries.definition: the study of how living bodies work. It looks like psychology but its root is physis 'nature'.
entries.definitionCN: 生理学；研究活体如何运作。它形似 psychology，但词根是 physis“自然”。

entries.definition: a personality disorder marked by lack of empathy. It shares psych- but ends in 'suffering'.
entries.definitionCN: 以缺乏共情为特征的人格障碍。它共享 psych-，但词尾是“痛苦”。

entries.definition: a person who studies the mind. It is the same word plus the agent suffix -ist.
entries.definitionCN: 心理学家。它是同一个词加上施事后缀 -ist。

entries.definition: the medical specialty that diagnoses and treats mental illness. It is clinical where psychology is academic.
entries.definitionCN: 诊断与治疗精神疾病的医学专科。它偏临床，而 psychology 偏学术。

entries.definition: the seat of thought, feeling and memory. It is the thing psychology studies, not the study.
entries.definitionCN: 思想、情感与记忆的所在。它是心理学研究的对象，而不是研究本身。

entries.definition: a person's or group's characteristic way of thinking. It matches the 'psychology of X' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 个人或群体特有的思维方式。它对应“X 的 psychology”这一义项。

entries.definition: the therapeutic method founded by Freud for exploring the unconscious. It is one school within psychology.
entries.definitionCN: 弗洛伊德创立、用于探索无意识的治疗方法。它是心理学内部的一个学派。

entries.definition: observable action and conduct. It is the evidence that modern psychology prefers to the soul.
entries.definitionCN: 可观察的行动与举止。它是现代心理学取代灵魂之后所偏好的证据。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Greek psykhē 'soul, breath', the -logia 'study' ending, and the modern split into psychiatry and psychoanalysis.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：希腊语 psykhē“灵魂、呼吸”、-logia“研究”词尾，以及现代分出的 psychiatry 与 psychoanalysis。

normal.en: psychology = psyche 'soul' + -logy 'study': first the soul, later the mind.
normal.cn: psychology = psyche“灵魂”+ -logy“研究”：先研究灵魂，后研究心智。

normal.en: Psyche was also the Greek girl loved by Eros, often drawn with butterfly wings — a soul with wings.
normal.cn: Psyche 还是希腊神话中被厄洛斯所爱的少女，常被画上蝶翼——一个长了翅膀的灵魂。

normal.en: Psychiatry treats the sick mind; psychology studies the mind in general. Same psyche, different second half.
normal.cn: psychiatry 治疗生病的心智；psychology 研究一般的心智。同一个 psyche，后半截不同。

normal.en: A psychologist is a psychologist; a psychiatrist is a doctor. The -ist and the -iatrist tell you.
normal.cn: psychologist 是心理学家；psychiatrist 是精神科医生。-ist 与 -iatrist 告诉你区别。

normal.en: Reverse psychology works because knowing the mind is already half of controlling it.
normal.cn: 反向心理之所以有效，是因为了解心智已经是控制它的一半。

abstract.en: The word is a mirror: it names both the study and the thing studied.
abstract.cn: 这个词是一面镜子：它既命名研究，也命名被研究之物。

abstract.en: It travels inward: from soul, to mind, to behavior, to the mind of a crowd.
abstract.cn: 它一路向内：从灵魂，到心智，到行为，再到人群的心。

abstract.en: Psychology is breath made legible: something invisible, turned into something you can describe.
abstract.cn: 心理学是把呼吸变得可读：某种看不见的东西，被转写成可以描述的东西。

examples.en: He took a course in psychology and started noticing his own habits.
examples.cn: 他上了一门心理学课程，开始注意到自己的习惯。

examples.en: The marketing team studies the psychology of impulse buying.
examples.cn: 营销团队研究冲动购物的心理。

examples.en: Using reverse psychology on a stubborn child often backfires.
examples.cn: 对固执的孩子使用反向心理，常常适得其反。

dict_mnemonic.text: psycho（心理）+ logy（学科）——研究心理的学问；谐音“赛可乐鸡”：赛前（psy）喝可乐（cho）吃鸡，琢磨对手心里想什么 → psychology 心理学；心理

root: 源自希腊语 psykhē“呼吸、灵魂、心灵”加 -logia“对……的研究”，经新拉丁语 psychologia 进入英语；核心是“对那口看不见的气息——灵魂与心智——的探究”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses around one object: the invisible mind. The word begins as the study of the soul, becomes the science of mental phenomena, then the mind of a person or crowd, a school of theory, a practical trick, a wartime weapon, and finally the inner life a novel reveals.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项围绕同一个对象：看不见的心智。这个词从“研究灵魂”开始，变成“研究心理现象的科学”，再指个人或群体的心理、一个理论学派、一种实用手段、一件战时武器，最后指小说所揭示的内心生活。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: leaning inward to listen to the breath-like mind and describe what it is doing.
core.cn: 核心意象：向内俯身，倾听那口气息般的心智，并描述它在做什么。

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINE: its birth as soul-study, its 1748 mind-science, and its 1890s behavioral form.
branches.cn: 学科：作为灵魂研究的诞生、1748 年的心理科学，以及 1890 年代的行为科学形态。

branches.en: THE MIND ITSELF: a person's makeup, a group's inner life, and a character's inner life in art.
branches.cn: 心智本身：个人的心理构成、群体的内心生活，以及艺术中人物的内心。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL: one theory-system among many, each with its own model of the mind.
branches.cn: 学派：众多理论体系中的一支，每一支都有自己的心灵模型。

branches.en: THE PRACTICAL TRICK: reading and steering a person in the moment.
branches.cn: 实用手段：当场读懂并引导一个人。

branches.en: THE WEAPON: psychology applied to morale, as psychological warfare.
branches.cn: 武器：作用于士气的心理学，即心理战。

intro.en: Psychology is psych- plus -ology. Its family shows the Greek root psych- 'soul, mind' and the suffix -logy 'study', plus the related endings -ologist, -ological and -iatry.
intro.cn: psychology 是 psych- 加 -ology。它的词族展示希腊词根 psych-“灵魂、心智”与后缀 -logy“研究”，以及相关词尾 -ologist、-ological、-iatry。

latinIntro.en: Greek psykhē 'soul, breath' is the base of psyche, psychology and psychiatry; Greek logos 'word, reason' supplies -logy, -logical and -logue.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 psykhē“灵魂、呼吸”是 psyche、psychology、psychiatry 的基础；希腊语 logos“言词、理性”提供 -logy、-logical、-logue。

items.example: Psychology explains why we forget names so easily.
items.exampleCN: 心理学解释了为什么我们那么容易忘记名字。

items.example: The poem explores the wounded psyche of a soldier.
items.exampleCN: 这首诗探索一名士兵受伤的心灵。

items.meaning: the medical treatment of mental illness
items.example: She trained in psychiatry before opening a clinic.
items.exampleCN: 她在开设诊所前接受了精神病学训练。

items.meaning: the Freudian method of exploring the unconscious
items.example: Psychoanalysis asks what a dream hides.
items.exampleCN: 精神分析追问一个梦隐藏了什么。

items.example: The school hired a psychologist for its students.
items.exampleCN: 学校为学生聘请了一位心理学家。

items.meaning: of the mind or of psychology
items.example: The injury was psychological rather than physical.
items.exampleCN: 这处伤是心理上的，而非身体上的。

items.meaning: a person with a severe personality disorder
items.example: The character is written as a charming psychopath.
items.exampleCN: 这个角色被写成一个有魅力的精神变态者。

items.meaning: having bodily symptoms caused by the mind
items.meaningCN: 心身性的（心智影响身体）
items.exampleCN: 压力可以引起心身性头痛。

items.meaning: the study of phenomena outside orthodox psychology

definition_en: the state of things as they actually exist; the quality of being real rather than imagined; the facts of a situation

senses.title: The world as it exists
senses.definition: the state of things as they actually exist, including what is unpleasant or unexpected
senses.definitionCN: 事物实际存在的情形，包括不愉快或出乎意料之处
senses.example: The reality of the job was harder than the advertisement suggested.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作的现实比广告上说的更难。
senses.why: Reality is real plus -ity, so it names the condition of being a thing that exists, not a wish or a picture.
senses.whyCN: reality 是 real 加 -ity，命名「作为存在之物的状态」，而非愿望或画面。

senses.title: Genuineness
senses.definition: the quality of being genuine, true or actual rather than imagined
senses.definitionCN: 真正、真实或实际而非想象的性质
senses.example: The documentary blurs the line between reality and fiction.
senses.exampleCN: 这部纪录片模糊了真实与虚构的界限。
senses.why: The same noun can point at the quality itself: how much of the real is in a thing.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也可指向性质本身：一物之中含有多少真实。

senses.title: Real life on screen
senses.definition: used as a modifier for programmes that show ordinary people in unscripted situations
senses.definitionCN: 用作定语，指展示普通人在无脚本情境中的节目
senses.example: Reality TV has changed what audiences expect from television.
senses.exampleCN: 真人秀改变了观众对电视的期待。
senses.why: Television borrowed the word for shows that claim to record real life rather than act it out.
senses.whyCN: 电视借用了这个词，指声称记录真实生活而非表演的节目。

intro.en: Reality is real with the Latin noun ending -ity, and its remote source is Latin res, a thing; it names the condition of being real.
intro.cn: reality 是 real 加拉丁名词词尾 -ity，其更早来源是拉丁语 res（事物）；它命名「真实的状况」。

items.en: Res meant a thing or a fact, the plain word for what exists.
items.cn: res 意为事物或事实，是「存在之物」的朴素说法。

items.en: Realitas meant the quality of being real, formed from realis with the noun ending -itas.
items.cn: realitas 意为真实的性质，由 realis 加名词词尾 -itas 构成。

items.en: English took the word as reality, keeping the sense of the way things actually stand.
items.cn: 英语把这个词借作 reality，保留「事物实际如何」的意思。

items.en: The word served for hard facts, then for television that claims to show life unscripted.
items.cn: 这个词先用于硬邦邦的事实，后用于声称展示无脚本生活的电视节目。

items.en: Modern English uses reality for the actual world, for genuineness, and for real-life television.
items.cn: 现代英语用 reality 指实际世界、真实性与真人生活类电视。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same root; the near-meaning group gathers words for fact and actual existence.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词根的词；近义组收表示事实与实际存在的词。

normal.en: Face reality means to accept facts you would rather avoid.

normal.en: A dream becomes a reality when it stops being only imagined.

definition_en: a person dearly loved; an affectionate form of address
core_image: 被捧在心口的称呼：对至亲之人的一声疼爱
scene: 奶奶在厨房门边招手，桌上刚出炉的饼干还冒着热气。" Come here, darling, and taste the biscuits," she smiled.
sceneCN: 这里 darling 是「亲爱的」（第 1 个义项：对至亲之人的亲昵称呼）；句意是奶奶招呼心爱的孩子来尝饼干。

pos.zh: 亲爱的；可爱的；讨人喜欢的

derivatives.zh: 基础词「亲爱的」，darling 由它加后缀构成
由 dear 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「深切地；珍爱地」
由 dear 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「亲爱；珍贵」

senses.title: A dearly loved person, as an address
senses.definition: someone you love very much, used when speaking to them
senses.definitionCN: 深受你爱的人，用作对本人说话时的称呼
senses.example: Goodnight, darling, sleep well.
senses.exampleCN: 晚安，亲爱的，睡个好觉。
senses.why: The suffix -ling turns 'dear' into a person: the one who is dear.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ling 把「亲爱的」变成「亲爱的人」，即被疼爱的那个人。

senses.title: A general friendly address, not only between lovers
senses.definition: a friendly or polite way of addressing someone you may barely know, especially in British speech
senses.definitionCN: 英式口语中对未必熟识的人的友好称呼，常出自店主、长辈之口
senses.example: "That's three pounds, darling," said the shopkeeper.
senses.exampleCN: 「一共三镑，亲爱的。」店主说道。
senses.why: Family warmth spills into public politeness; the affectionate word becomes a social habit.
senses.whyCN: 家庭的温情溢出到公共礼貌中，亲昵称呼成了社交习惯。

senses.title: A person or thing especially favoured by a group
senses.definition: someone who is the current favourite of the public, media, or a community
senses.definitionCN: 公众、媒体或某群体当下最宠爱的人或事物
senses.example: The young actress quickly became the darling of the critics.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻女演员很快成了评论界的宠儿。
senses.why: Being loved by one person generalises into being loved by everyone, hence 'favourite'.
senses.whyCN: 「被一个人疼爱」推广为「被众人宠爱」，于是有了「宠儿」义。

senses.title: Charming or delightful (adjective)
senses.titleCN: 可爱的；讨人喜欢的（形容词）
senses.definition: attractive in a charming, endearing way
senses.definitionCN: 以迷人、惹人疼爱的样子吸引人的
senses.example: What a darling little hat she is wearing!
senses.exampleCN: 她戴的这顶小帽子真可爱！
senses.why: The feeling one has for a loved person transfers to anything that charms the same way.
senses.whyCN: 对心爱之人的情感转移到同样惹人怜爱的物件上，称呼词便转作形容词。

intro.en: Darling is dear plus the Old English person suffix -ling, a purely Germanic formation.
intro.cn: darling 是 dear 加古英语人称后缀 -ling 构成，纯日耳曼构词。

items.en: The reconstructed root *dēuz- or *dairiz is not secure; 'dear' is generally linked to a root meaning precious or valued, related to Old Norse dýrr.
items.cn: 「dear」的重构词根一般与「珍贵、有价值」义相关，与古诺斯语 dýrr 同源，重构形式，具体来源存疑。

items.en: Old English dēore meant dear or precious, and the suffix -ling made person words such as deorling, already used for a loved one.
items.cn: 古英语 dēore 意为「亲爱的、珍贵的」；后缀 -ling 构成人称词，deorling 一形已用于指心爱之人。

items.en: Middle English dereling and darling spread as a term for a beloved person, in both romance and family contexts.
items.cn: 中古英语 dereling、darling 广泛用于指心爱之人，涵盖爱情与家庭语境。

items.en: Shakespeare's plays use darling both as address and as adjective; the 'favourite of a group' sense begins to appear.
items.cn: 莎士比亚剧作中 darling 已兼作称呼与形容词；「群体宠儿」义开始出现。

items.en: Modern British speech keeps it as a friendly address to strangers, while media language calls celebrities the darlings of a group.
items.cn: 现代英式口语保留了对陌生人的友好称呼用法，媒体语言则称名人为何种群体的 darling。

note.en: Darling sits in a family of -ling person words and a group of affectionate addresses; separate it from look-alike darning.
note.cn: darling 属于 -ling 人称后缀词族和亲昵称呼词群；注意与形近的 darning 区分。

intro.cn: darling 由形容词 dear 加人称后缀 -ling 构成；其词族展示英语如何为「被爱者、幼小者」命名。

latinIntro.en: Darling has no Latin ancestry; both dear and -ling are Germanic, so no Latin relatives are listed.
latinIntro.cn: darling 无拉丁语来源；dear 与 -ling 均为日耳曼成分，因此不列拉丁同族词。

items.meaningCN: 亲爱的、珍贵的，darling 的词基

items.meaning: one connected with; a young one
items.meaningCN: 古英语后缀，构成「某类人」或「幼崽」
darling 的古英语前身，义为「心爱的人」

items.example: the twins are mother's little darlings
items.exampleCN: 双胞胎是妈妈的小宝贝。

items.meaningCN: 「织补」，形近词，词源与 darling 无关
深切地；由基础词 dear 派生

definition_zh: 民主；民主制度；民主国家
definition_en: a system in which people choose their leaders and share the power to decide
core_image: 广场上无数只手同时举起，每只手都握着同样一张票
scene: 投票站门口排起长队，老人拄着拐杖也要自己走进去投一票。 A democracy depends on people who are willing to show up.
sceneCN: 这里 democracy 指「民主制度」（第 1 个义项：由人民选择领导者并分享决定权的制度）；句意是民主制度依靠那些愿意站出来的人。

pos.zh: 民主；民主制度；民主国家

senses.title: Rule by the people
senses.definition: a system of government in which adults choose their leaders by voting
senses.definitionCN: 成年人通过投票选择领导者的政治制度
senses.example: The country chose democracy after years of struggle.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家经过多年斗争选择了民主制度。
senses.why: Power is lent by many hands and can be taken back by the same hands.
senses.whyCN: 权力由许多只手借出，也能被同样多的手收回。

senses.title: A country run that way
senses.definition: a country whose government is chosen in free elections
senses.definitionCN: 通过自由选举产生政府的国家
senses.example: New democracies often rewrite their rules in the first years.
senses.exampleCN: 新的民主国家常在最初几年改写自己的规则。
senses.why: A place that lives by a system ends up wearing its name.
senses.whyCN: 按一种制度生活的地方，最后也会戴上它的名字。

senses.title: Fair voice in daily life
senses.definition: the habit of giving every person an equal say
senses.definitionCN: 让每个人都拥有同等发言权的习惯
senses.example: She brought a little democracy into the family meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她给家庭会议带来了一点民主精神。
senses.why: The word leaves the ballot box and enters any room where voices are counted.
senses.whyCN: 这个词走出投票箱，进入任何需要数人头的房间。

intro.en: Democracy comes from Greek demos, the people, and kratia, rule; French carried it into English.
intro.cn: democracy 来自希腊语 demos（人民）与 kratia（统治），经法语进入英语。

items.en: Demos named the common people, and kratia named rule or strength.
items.cn: demos 指普通民众，kratia 指统治或力量。

items.en: Athens called its assembly-run city a demokratia.
items.cn: 雅典把由公民大会治理的城邦称为 demokratia。

items.en: Roman writers discussed the Greek idea but ruled through a republic.
items.cn: 罗马作家讨论过这个希腊观念，却以共和制来统治。

items.en: English borrowed democracy to name rule by the many.
items.cn: 英语借来 democracy，用来指多数人的统治。

items.en: It now also means a fair voice in schools, clubs and homes.
items.cn: 如今它也指学校、社团与家庭中的平等发言权。

note.en: The look-alike group all begin with demo-, and the meaning group turns from a form of state to the simple idea of equal voice.
note.cn: 形近组都以 demo- 开头，近义组则从国家形式转到平等发言这个朴素观念。

entries.definition: a person who believes in rule by the people
entries.definitionCN: 相信人民统治的人

entries.definition: based on equal power for all people
entries.definitionCN: 建立在人人平等权力之上的

entries.definition: the study of populations
entries.definitionCN: 对人口的研究

entries.definition: a state with an elected head, not a king
entries.definitionCN: 元首由选举产生而非君主的国家

entries.definition: the right of a group to rule itself
entries.definitionCN: 群体自我治理的权利

entries.definition: the state of being treated the same
entries.definitionCN: 被同等对待的状态

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a raised hand in a square and end with a vote that can be taken back.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从广场上举起的一只手开始，落到一张可以被收回的选票。

normal.en: One person, one paper slip: the whole idea fits in a palm.
normal.cn: 一人一张纸，整套道理就握在掌心里。

normal.en: A ruler who fears the count will try to stop the counting.
normal.cn: 害怕数人头的统治者，总会想办法阻止清点。

normal.en: Democracy is loud on voting day and quiet in between.
normal.cn: 民主在投票日很响，在平常日子很静。

normal.en: The word is Greek, but the queue at the polling station is local.
normal.cn: 这个词是希腊的，投票站前的队伍却是本地的。

normal.en: A club, a class, a family: any room can hold a small democracy.
normal.cn: 社团、班级、家庭，任何一间屋子都能装下小小的民主。

abstract.en: Picture a square full of hands lifted at the same height.
abstract.cn: 想象一个广场，无数只手举到同样的高度。

abstract.en: Picture a box sealed, then opened, then counted in public.
abstract.cn: 想象一只箱子被封上、打开，再当众清点。

abstract.en: Picture a chair left empty because the voters chose someone else.
abstract.cn: 想象一把椅子空着，因为选民选了别人。

examples.en: The country chose democracy after years of struggle.
examples.cn: 这个国家经过多年斗争选择了民主制度。

examples.en: New democracies often rewrite their rules in the first years.
examples.cn: 新的民主国家常在最初几年改写自己的规则。

examples.en: A healthy democracy needs more than one loud voice.
examples.cn: 健康的民主制度需要不止一个响亮的声音。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 democracy 记成「得莫克拉西」：demos 是人民，kratia 是统治，人民来统治，就是民主。

root: 来自希腊语 demokratia，由 demos（人民）与 kratia（统治）组成，经法语进入英语。本义是由人民来统治，后来既指制度，也指实行这种制度的国家，又引申为日常生活中的平等精神。

sensesIntro.en: From many hands choosing a leader, to the country they build, to the small fairness of an ordinary room.
sensesIntro.cn: 从许多只手选出领导者，到他们建起的国家，再到普通房间里的一点公平。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a square full of raised hands, one vote in each.
core.cn: 核心意象：广场上举起一片手，每只手里一张票。

branches.en: The first sense is the machine: votes choose the people who decide.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是那台机器：选票决定由谁来作决定。

branches.en: The second sense is the country that runs on that machine.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是靠这台机器运转的国家。

branches.en: The third sense is the habit, carried into small rooms.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是被带进小房间里的那种习惯。

branches.en: A system and a state share one name because the state is the system at work.
branches.cn: 制度与国家共用一个名字，因为国家就是运转中的制度。

branches.en: A country and a club both need the same small courtesy: let others speak.
branches.cn: 国家和社团都需要同一种小小的礼貌：让别人说话。

intro.en: Democracy has a Greek skeleton and grows words for believers, changes and the study of populations.
intro.cn: democracy 有一副希腊骨架，长出了表示信奉者、变革与人口研究的词。

latinIntro.en: The Greek pieces are demos, the people, and kratia, rule; Latin kept the idea rather than the word.
latinIntro.cn: 它的希腊零件是 demos（人民）与 kratia（统治）；拉丁语留下的是观念，不是这个词。

items.exampleCN: 民主制度需要耐心的公民。

items.meaning: a believer in rule by the people
items.exampleCN: 她一生都是民主主义者。

items.meaning: based on equal power for all
in a fair and equal way
items.exampleCN: 领导者是以民主方式选出的。

items.meaning: to make something open to all

definition_zh: 包裹；邮包；一块土地；把……包起来；分派
definition_en: something wrapped in paper or packed in a box and sent by post, a measured area of land, or to wrap goods and divide them into portions
core_image: 柜台上一只牛皮纸包被麻绳捆成十字，收件地址写在正面
scene: 邮局柜台前，店员把一只用麻绳捆好的纸包推过来，又把票据压在下面。 He collected the parcel from the counter and checked the address.
sceneCN: 这里的 parcel 是「包裹、邮包」（第 1 个义项：包好待寄送的东西）；句意是他从柜台上取回包裹，又核对了地址。图中可辨识物件：麻绳、牛皮纸包、票据。

derivatives.zh: 由 parcel 双写 l 加 -ing 构成，义为「打包；分块的方式」
由 parcel 与 post 复合而成，义为「包裹邮政」
由 parcel 与 bomb 复合而成，义为「邮包炸弹」

senses.title: Something wrapped and sent by post
senses.definition: something wrapped in paper, tied with string or packed in a box, especially for sending by post
senses.definitionCN: 用纸包好、用绳捆上或装进盒子，尤指通过邮局寄送的东西
senses.example: He collected the parcel from the counter and checked the address.
senses.exampleCN: 他从柜台上取回包裹，又核对了地址。
senses.why: Parcel began as Latin particula, a small part, and French used it for a small piece of anything; an item tied up for the post was simply one such piece.
senses.whyCN: parcel 最初是拉丁语 particula，意为「一小部分」，法语用它指任何东西的一小块；寄送时捆好的那件东西，不过是这样的「一块」而已。

senses.title: A measured piece of land
senses.definition: a piece of land, especially one marked out for a particular use or owned as a single unit
senses.definitionCN: 一块土地，尤指划作某种用途或作为一个单位拥有的地块
senses.example: They bought a small parcel of land beside the river.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在河边买下了一小块地。
senses.why: If a parcel is a portion cut from a whole, land can be divided the same way, so the word came to name one plot marked on a surveyor's map.
senses.whyCN: 既然 parcel 是从整体里切出的一份，土地也能这样切分，于是这个词用来指测量图上标好的一个地块。

senses.title: To wrap something up
senses.definition: to wrap goods in paper or another material and fasten them, often before sending
senses.definitionCN: 把货物用纸或其他材料包好并捆紧，通常是为了寄送
senses.example: She parcelled the books and took them to the post office.
senses.exampleCN: 她把书包好，送到邮局去。
senses.why: The noun named the finished bundle, so the verb simply names the act of producing it: to parcel is to turn loose goods into one tied package.
senses.whyCN: 名词指的是包好的成品，动词便直接指做出这个成品的动作：parcel 就是把散着的东西变成一只捆好的包。

senses.title: To divide into shares
senses.definition: to divide something into portions and give them out, usually in the phrase parcel out
senses.definitionCN: 把某物分成若干份分发出去，通常用于 parcel out 这一说法
senses.example: The land was parcelled out among the villagers.
senses.exampleCN: 这块地被分给了村民们。
senses.why: Because the word already meant a portion, parcel out reverses the picture: instead of gathering things into one bundle, it cuts the whole into separate shares.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本来就指「一份」，parcel out 于是把画面翻了过来：不再把东西收进一只包，而是把整体切成一份份拿出去。

intro.en: Parcel comes from Old French parcelle, a small piece, which is a diminutive of Latin particula, itself a small form of pars, part; English first used it for a portion and only later for a package and a plot of land.
intro.cn: parcel 来自古法语 parcelle（一小块），它是拉丁语 particula 的指小形式，而 particula 又是 pars（部分）的小称；英语先用它指「一份」，后来才指包裹与地块。

items.en: Pars meant a part or a share, and it is the ultimate source of a whole family of English words about portions.
items.cn: pars 意为部分、份额，是英语中一整族表示「份」的词的最终来源。

items.en: Particula was the small form of pars, so it named a little part or a tiny piece of something.
items.cn: particula 是 pars 的小称，指一小部分或某物的一小块。

items.en: Old French kept the word as parcelle and used it for a small piece or a portion of a larger whole.
items.cn: 古法语把它保留为 parcelle，用来指一小块或整体中的一份。

items.en: Middle English parcel first meant a part or a portion, and it could name a piece of land as well as a share of goods.
items.cn: 中古英语的 parcel 最初指部分或一份，既能指一块地，也能指一份货物。

items.en: Modern English made the wrapped item the main sense, kept the land sense, and added the verb meanings of wrapping and dividing.
items.cn: 现代英语把包好的东西变成主要义项，保留土地义，又添上「包起来」与「分成份」两个动词义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Latin root for part, so the split between parcel and the partial family is visible; the near-meaning group gathers words for wrapped goods.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「部分」词根上的词，方便看清 parcel 与 partial 一族的分叉；近义组收表示包好的货物的词。

entries.definition: A very small piece of matter; both words descend from Latin particula.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的物质颗粒；两个词都出自拉丁语 particula。

entries.definition: Covering only a part, or favouring one side; from Latin pars.
entries.definitionCN: 只涉及一部分的，或偏袒一方的；出自拉丁语 pars。

entries.definition: One specific thing rather than any other; from Latin particula.
entries.definitionCN: 特定的那一个，而不是别的；出自拉丁语 particula。

entries.definition: To take a share of something, as in partake of a meal.
entries.definitionCN: 分享一份，如 partake of a meal 指一同进餐。

entries.definition: Something wrapped or boxed, especially for sending or selling.
entries.definitionCN: 包好或装箱的东西，尤指寄送或出售的。

entries.definition: A small paper or plastic container holding a measured amount.
entries.definitionCN: 装一定量物品的纸或塑料小袋。

entries.definition: A number of things tied or wrapped together.
entries.definitionCN: 捆在一起或包在一起的一堆东西。

entries.definition: A load of goods sent to someone, especially for sale.
entries.definitionCN: 发运给某人的一批货物，尤指出售用。

normalIntro.en: Parcel is a word for a piece cut from a whole, and its hooks follow that piece from a share of land to a bundle tied for the post.
normalIntro.cn: parcel 是一个表示「从整体中切下的一块」的词，记忆钩子顺着这块东西，从一份土地走到捆好待寄的包裹。

normal.en: Parcel descends from Latin pars, part, through particula and Old French parcelle, so a parcel is literally a little part.
normal.cn: parcel 经由 particula 与古法语 parcelle 上溯拉丁语 pars（部分），所以它字面上就是「一小块」。

normal.en: A parcel of land keeps the oldest sense visible: a measured share of ground, not a thing you mail.
normal.cn: a parcel of land 保留了最古老的义项：量好的一份地，而不是寄出去的东西。

normal.en: Parcel out reverses the picture of a tied bundle: the whole is cut into portions instead of being gathered into one.
normal.cn: parcel out 把捆成一只包的画面翻了过来：整体被切成若干份，而不是被收进一只包。

normal.en: Part and parcel uses the old sense of a share to say that something is an inseparable piece of a larger thing.
normal.cn: part and parcel 用的是「一份」的旧义，表示某物是更大整体中不可分割的一块。

normal.en: The British verb doubles the l as parcelled, while the American spelling keeps one l as parceled.
normal.cn: 英式动词双写 l 写作 parcelled，美式拼写只留一个 l，写作 parceled。

abstract.en: A word that means both a mailed package and a plot of land suggests that owning and sending are both matters of pieces.
abstract.cn: 一个词既指邮寄的包裹又指一块地，说明拥有与投递都与「份」有关。

abstract.en: Because parcel began as a small part, every parcel still carries the idea of a whole that has been divided.
abstract.cn: 因为 parcel 起初指一小部分，所以每一只包裹至今都带着「整体被分割过」的意思。

abstract.en: To parcel out land or money is to admit that a whole cannot stay whole once it belongs to several people.
abstract.cn: 把土地或钱分派出去，等于承认整体一旦归几个人所有，就再也无法保持完整。

examples.en: He collected the parcel from the counter and checked the address.
examples.cn: 他从柜台上取回包裹，又核对了地址。

examples.en: They bought a small parcel of land beside the river.
examples.cn: 他们在河边买下了一小块地。

examples.en: The land was parcelled out among the villagers.
examples.cn: 这块地被分给了村民们。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕搜」——邮局里的人怕搜，先把东西捆成一包再递出去；记住 parcel 是包裹，也指一块地。

root: 拉丁语 pars（部分）经小称 particula 与古法语 parcelle 进入英语；同族有 particle、partial、particular，词义从「一小份」分叉出「包好的一件」「一块地」「分成份」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a piece cut from a whole; the senses divide into the piece tied for the post, the piece of ground, the act of wrapping, and the act of dividing.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是从整体中切下的一块；义项按「捆好待寄的那一件」「一块地」「包起来的动作」「分成份的动作」分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brown paper parcel crossed by string, an address written on the front.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只牛皮纸包被麻绳捆成十字，正面写着收件地址。

branches.en: a wrapped parcel pushed across a post office counter
branches.cn: 从邮局柜台上推过来的一只包裹

branches.en: an address in ink on brown paper
branches.cn: 牛皮纸上用墨水写下的地址

branches.en: a strip of riverside field marked on a map
branches.cn: 地图上标出的河边一条田地

branches.en: string pulled tight and knotted around paper
branches.cn: 绳子在纸上拉紧打结

branches.en: a field cut into narrow strips for several families
branches.cn: 一块地被切成细条分给几户人家

intro.en: Latin pars and its small form particula supply the meaning of a piece, French passes the word on, and two English suffixes build the noun and the action.
intro.cn: 拉丁语 pars 及其小称 particula 提供「一块」的含义，法语把词传给英语，两个英语后缀再把它变成名词与动作。

latinIntro.en: Both Latin pars and particula are recorded, so this word has a reliable Latin ancestry shared with particle, partial and particular.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pars 与 particula 均有记录，因此这个词有可靠的拉丁世系，并与 particle、partial、particular 同源。

items.meaning: a wrapped package or a plot of land
to wrap or to divide into shares

definition_en: a person who is paid to work for a company or another person
core_image: 胸前的员工卡，证明自己在这家单位工作
scene: 每位员工都收到一份新合同。 Every employee received a new contract.
sceneCN: 这里 employee 是「员工」（第 1 个义项：被单位付钱雇用的人）；句意：每位员工都收到一份新合同。

senses.title: A person who works for pay
senses.definition: someone who is hired and paid to do work for another person or organization
senses.definitionCN: 被雇用并领取报酬、为他人或组织工作的人
senses.example: The company has over two hundred employees.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司有两百多名员工。
senses.why: The ending -ee marks the receiver of the action, so the employee is the one taken into work.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ee 标记动作的承受者，因此 employee 是被纳入工作的一方。

senses.title: A member of a workforce
senses.definition: a person counted as part of the staff of a workplace
senses.definitionCN: 被算作某个工作单位员工队伍一员的人
senses.example: Every employee must wear a badge.
senses.exampleCN: 每位员工都必须佩戴工牌。
senses.why: In a workplace the word also names a role in the group, not only a contract.
senses.whyCN: 在工作场所，这个词不仅指一份契约，也指群体中的一个角色。

intro.en: Employee is employ plus the French ending -ee, meaning the one who receives the action.
intro.cn: employee 是 employ 加法语词尾 -ee，意为动作的承受者。

items.en: The ending -e forms past participles that can name a person.
items.cn: 古法语词尾 -e 构成可指人的过去分词。

items.en: Employé names a person who is employed.
items.cn: employé 指被雇用的人。

items.en: English borrows the word as employee or employé.
items.cn: 英语借入时写作 employee 或 employé。

items.en: Employee becomes common with factories and offices.
items.cn: 随着工厂与办公室的兴起，employee 变得常用。

items.en: Employee is the standard word for a paid worker.
items.cn: 现代英语中，employee 是有薪工作者的标准说法。

note.en: An employee works for an employer; a worker is broader, and staff names the group.
note.cn: employee 为 employer 工作；worker 范围更广，staff 指员工群体。

entries.definitionCN: 雇主，雇用员工的一方

definition_zh: 工业的；产业的；工业化的；从事工业的
definition_en: relating to industry, manufacturing, or the people and systems that produce goods in factories
core_image: 厂房里的传送带不停转动，成品排成队列向外送出
scene: 沿河的老厂房连成一片，烟囱林立，机器声日夜不停。 The industrial belt along the river employed half the town.
sceneCN: 这里 industrial 是「工业的」（第 1 个义项：与工业或制造业相关的）；句意：沿河的工业带雇用了镇上半数人口；它的老纺织厂如今与新电子厂并立。图中可辨识物件：厂房、传送带、烟囱、电子元件。

pos.zh: 工业的；产业的；工业化的；从事工业的

senses.title: Relating to industry and manufacturing
senses.definition: connected with industry, especially the manufacturing of goods in factories
senses.definitionCN: 与工业相关的，尤指在工厂中制造商品
senses.example: The government published a report on industrial growth.
senses.exampleCN: 政府发布了一份关于工业增长的报告。
senses.why: Latin -alis means 'of or pertaining to'. Added to industry, industrial simply means 'of industry'; when industry came to mean factory manufacturing, the adjective followed it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 -alis 意为「属于某物的、与某物相关的」。加在 industry 上，industrial 就是「工业的」；当 industry 转指工厂制造业时，这个形容词也随之转义。

senses.title: Used in or for industry
senses.definition: made for use by industry, or operating on the scale of industry rather than a household
senses.definitionCN: 供工业使用的，或按工业而非家庭规模运作的
senses.example: Industrial chemicals must be stored under strict safety rules.
senses.exampleCN: 工业化学品必须在严格的安全规则下储存。
senses.why: The adjective marks belonging: chemicals that belong to the industrial process, not the kitchen. The same pattern gives industrial diamonds and industrial glue.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标记归属：属于工业流程而非厨房的化学品。同一模式也构成 industrial diamonds（工业钻石）与 industrial glue（工业胶）。

senses.title: Having a lot of industry
senses.titleCN: 工业发达的；工业密集的
senses.definition: describing a place that contains many factories and much manufacturing
senses.definitionCN: 描述一个拥有许多工厂和大量制造业的地方
senses.example: The industrial north has higher wages but worse air.
senses.exampleCN: 工业化的北方工资更高，但空气更差。
senses.why: A place can be named by what fills it. If industry fills a region, the region is industrial, just as a forested valley is wooded.
senses.whyCN: 一个地方可以用充满它的东西来命名。如果工业充满一个地区，这个地区就是 industrial，正如长满森林的山谷是 wooded。

senses.title: Relating to employers and workers
senses.definition: concerning the relationship between employers and employees, especially disputes and negotiations
senses.definitionCN: 关于雇主与雇员之间关系的，尤指争端与谈判
senses.example: Industrial relations in the plant have improved since the new manager arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 新经理到任后，厂里的劳资关系有所改善。
senses.why: The relationship exists inside industry, so the adjective locates it: industrial relations are the relations of the industrial workplace, not relations between industries.
senses.whyCN: 这种关系存在于工业内部，所以形容词为其定位：industrial relations 是工业工作场所内部的关系，而非工业之间的关系。

senses.title: Concerning government policy toward industry
senses.definition: relating to official plans and measures that support, regulate, or restructure industry
senses.definitionCN: 与支持、规范或重组工业的官方计划与措施相关的
senses.example: Industrial policy in the region focuses on semiconductors.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的产业政策聚焦于半导体。
senses.why: Here industrial marks the object of policy: the policy is about industry. The adjective tells you what the noun governs, not who makes it.
senses.whyCN: 此处 industrial 标记政策的对象：政策是关于工业的。这个形容词说明名词管的是什么，而不是谁制定它。

senses.title: Characteristic of an industrial society
senses.titleCN: 工业社会的；工业时代的
senses.definition: belonging to the era or type of society whose economy and daily life are dominated by industry
senses.definitionCN: 属于经济与日常生活由工业主导的时代或社会类型的
senses.example: The industrial city replaced the market town as the typical settlement.
senses.exampleCN: 工业城市取代集镇成为典型的聚居形态。
senses.why: When industry dominates an age, the adjective can name the age itself: industrial society is the society shaped by industry, a label rather than a description of a single object.
senses.whyCN: 当工业主导一个时代时，这个形容词可以命名时代本身：industrial society 是由工业塑造的社会，是标签而非对单一事物的描述。

senses.title: Belonging to the secondary sector
senses.titleCN: 第二产业的；工业部门的
senses.definition: belonging to the sector of the economy that transforms raw materials into goods, as opposed to agriculture or services
senses.definitionCN: 属于把原材料转化为产品的经济部门，与农业或服务业相对
senses.example: Industrial employment fell as service jobs expanded.
senses.exampleCN: 随着服务业岗位扩张，工业就业下降。
senses.why: Statisticians classify an economy by adjectives: agricultural, industrial, service. The adjective turns a sector into a label, and the label becomes a noun-like category.
senses.whyCN: 统计学家用形容词给经济分类：农业的、工业的、服务业的。这个形容词把部门变成标签，而标签又近似名词范畴。

senses.title: Industrial shares on the stock market
senses.definition: the shares of industrial companies, used in the plural as a category on financial markets
senses.definitionCN: 工业公司的股票，在金融市场上以复数形式作为一类资产
senses.example: Investors moved money out of industrials and into technology.
senses.exampleCN: 投资者把资金从工业股转投科技股。
senses.why: This is an ellipsis: 'industrial shares' loses shares and keeps the adjective, which then behaves as a noun. English does this with many adjectives, as in valuables and chemicals.
senses.whyCN: 这是省略：industrial shares 省去 shares，只留形容词，形容词便充当名词。英语常用这种方式，如 valuables 与 chemicals。

senses.title: Bare, functional, machine-made in style
senses.titleCN: 工业风的；机器制造感的
senses.definition: having a plain, functional, machine-made look, as in industrial design or industrial music
senses.definitionCN: 具有朴素、功能化、机器制造观感的，如工业设计或工业音乐
senses.example: The loft kept its industrial look with exposed pipes and concrete walls.
senses.exampleCN: 这间 Loft 保留工业风，露出管道和混凝土墙。
senses.why: The metaphor drops the factory and keeps its manner: what looks as if it came from a factory, all bare function and metal, is called industrial.
senses.whyCN: 这个隐喻丢开工厂本身，只保留它的方式：看起来像从工厂出来、全是裸露功能与金属感的东西，就被称为 industrial。

intro.en: Industrial is industry plus the Latin adjective suffix -alis, which became English -al. French industriel was the model for the English word, and the manufacturing sense of industry made the adjective mean 'of factories'.
intro.cn: industrial 是 industry 加拉丁形容词后缀 -alis（在英语中变为 -al）构成。法语 industriel 是英语词的样板；industry 的制造业义使这个形容词意为「工厂的」。

items.en: industria meant 'diligence, activity, care'. Its deeper origin is uncertain and is generally reconstructed as indu- (in-) + struere 'to build', but this is not proven.
items.cn: industria 意为「勤勉、活动、用心」。其更深来源不确定，一般重构为 indu-（in-）+ struere「建造」，但并未得到证明。

items.en: industrius meant 'diligent, active'. It kept the personal sense of hard work, which English preserves in industrious.
items.cn: industrius 意为「勤勉的、活跃的」。它保留了个人勤奋这一意义，英语以 industrious 保存下来。

items.en: 18th-century French formed industriel from industrie to mean 'relating to manufacturing'. French was then the language of economic writing, so the model spread quickly.
items.cn: 18 世纪法语由 industrie 构成 industriel，意为「与制造业相关的」。当时法语是经济写作的语言，这一样板迅速传播。

items.en: English adopted industrial in the late 18th century, at first in phrases describing manufacturing. The word grew with the very thing it described.
items.cn: 英语在 18 世纪晚期采用 industrial，最初用于描述制造业的短语。这个词随它所描述的事物一同成长。

items.en: The phrase industrial revolution made the adjective the name of an era. From there industrial society, industrial city, and industrial age followed as standard labels.
items.cn: industrial revolution 这一短语使该形容词成为时代的名称。此后 industrial society、industrial city、industrial age 都成为标准标签。

items.en: In the 20th century industrial produced a noun plural, industrials, for industrial shares, and later described machine-made styles in design and music. These are ellipses and metaphors of the core sense.
items.cn: 20 世纪 industrial 产生名词复数 industrials，指工业股票；后来又在设计与音乐中描述机器制造的风格。这些都是核心义的省略与隐喻。

note.en: Group one shares the Latin base industria; group two is close in meaning but not cognate with it (manus + facere, Greek mekhane, and the compound mass-produce).
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁词基 industria；第二组意义相近，但与它并非同源（manus + facere、希腊 mekhane，以及复合词 mass-produce）。

entries.definition: manufacturing as a sector, or diligent work; the noun from which industrial is formed
entries.definitionCN: 作为部门的制造业，或勤勉的工作；industrial 所由构成的名词

entries.definition: hard-working; it kept the 'diligence' sense of industria and never came to mean 'of factories'
entries.definitionCN: 勤劳的；它保留了 industria 的「勤勉」义，从未变成「工厂的」

entries.definition: having developed a large manufacturing base; the -ed form describes a result, while industrial describes a relation
entries.definitionCN: 已发展出大规模制造业的；-ed 形式描述结果，而 industrial 描述关系

entries.definition: an owner or manager of large industry; -ist names a person, not a quality
entries.definitionCN: 大型工业的所有者或管理者；-ist 命名人，而非性质

entries.definition: the making of goods on a large scale; it names the activity, while industrial describes what belongs to it
entries.definitionCN: 大规模制造商品；它命名活动，而 industrial 描述从属于该活动的事物

entries.definition: run or operated by machines; a mechanized process is one kind of industrial process
entries.definitionCN: 由机器运行或操作的；机械化的过程是工业过程的一种

entries.definition: made in large numbers by a standard process; it stresses quantity, not the whole industrial system
entries.definitionCN: 按标准流程大量制造的；强调数量，而非整个工业体系

entries.definition: relating to manual or factory workers; it describes people, while industrial can describe places, goods, or policies
entries.definitionCN: 与体力或工厂劳动者相关的；它描述人，而 industrial 可描述地点、商品或政策

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes and real word relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分和真实同族词。

normal.en: industria 'diligence, activity' + -al 'of or pertaining to': industrial means 'of that activity', and the activity later became factory manufacturing.
normal.cn: industria「勤勉、活动」+ -al「与之相关的」：industrial 意为「与该活动相关的」，而该活动后来变成了工厂制造。

normal.en: Keep industrial and industrious apart: industrial is about factories, industrious is about hard work. The same root took two roads.
normal.cn: 把 industrial 与 industrious 分清：前者关于工厂，后者关于勤奋。同一词根走了两条路。

normal.en: The family runs industry → industrial → industrialize → industrialization, one suffix at a time.
normal.cn: 这个词族沿 industry → industrial → industrialize → industrialization 展开，每次加一个后缀。

normal.en: A skyline of smokestacks and conveyor belts is an industrial skyline; the adjective paints the whole scene.
normal.cn: 由烟囱和传送带构成的天际线就是 industrial 天际线；这个形容词把整个场景涂上颜色。

normal.en: The industrial revolution is the phrase that turned the adjective into the name of an age.
normal.cn: industrial revolution 这一短语把这个形容词变成了一个时代的名称。

abstract.en: Think of a conveyor belt as the spine of a factory: whatever the belt touches becomes industrial.
abstract.cn: 把传送带想象成工厂的脊椎：传送带碰到什么，什么就变成工业的。

abstract.en: Think of two words leaving one root: industrious stays with the worker's sweat, industrial walks into the factory.
abstract.cn: 想象两个词从同一词根出发：industrious 留在工人的汗水里，industrial 走进工厂。

abstract.en: Think of a map coloured grey wherever chimneys stand; that grey is the adjective's territory.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，凡有烟囱处就涂成灰色；这片灰色就是该形容词的领地。

examples.en: The Ruhr became the industrial heart of Germany in the nineteenth century.
examples.cn: 鲁尔区在 19 世纪成为德国的工业心脏。

examples.en: Industrial action halted production for two weeks.
examples.cn: 工业行动使生产停顿了两周。

examples.en: Industrial design favours clean lines and cheap materials.
examples.cn: 工业设计偏爱简洁线条与廉价材料。

dict_mnemonic.note: 拆词联想 · 词源辅助
dict_mnemonic.text: industry（工业）+ -al（表所属）→ industrial 工业的；同根 industrious 却是「勤劳的」——一个进工厂，一个留在人身上

root: 拉丁 industria「勤勉、活动」+ 拉丁形容词后缀 -alis（英语 -al）；industria 一般认为是 indu-（in）+ struere「建造」。同根词 industrious 保留「勤奋」义，industrial 则沿「制造业」义发展。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses spread outward from 'of industry': the inputs industry uses, the places and eras it dominates, the relations inside it, the policies about it, its shares, and finally its machine-made look.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从「工业的」向外铺开：工业使用的投入品、它主导的地点与时代、它内部的劳资关系、关于它的政策、它的股票，最后是它机器制造的观感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a conveyor belt that never stops, turning material into finished goods.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条不停运转、把材料变成成品的传送带。

branches.en: THE CORE RELATION: what belongs to industry, including the materials and processes industry uses.
branches.cn: 核心关系：从属于工业的事物，包括工业使用的材料与流程。

branches.en: PLACE, ERA, SECTOR: regions filled with industry, industrial civilization, and the industrial sector of an economy.
branches.cn: 地点、时代与部门：布满工业的地区、工业文明，以及经济中的工业部门。

branches.en: WORKPLACE AND POLICY: relations between employers and workers, and government policy toward industry.
branches.cn: 劳资与政策：雇主与工人之间的关系，以及政府对工业的政策。

branches.en: FINANCE: industrials are the shares of industrial companies, an ellipsis of 'industrial shares'.
branches.cn: 金融：industrials 指工业公司的股票，是 industrial shares 的省略。

branches.en: STYLE: bare, functional, machine-made design is called industrial by metaphor.
branches.cn: 风格：朴素、功能化、机器制造的设计被隐喻地称为工业风。

intro.en: Industrial is a single suffix added to a noun: industry + -al. The suffix is Latin -alis, the ordinary maker of 'belonging to' adjectives, also seen in natural, national, and cultural.
intro.cn: industrial 只是名词加一个后缀：industry + -al。该后缀是拉丁 -alis，是构成表示所属关系的形容词的常规手段，也见于 natural、national、cultural。

latinIntro.en: Latin industria 'diligence' yielded both the personal adjective industrius and, much later, the manufacturing noun industry. The root appears as industr-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 industria「勤勉」既产出了描述人的形容词 industrius，也在很久以后产出了表示制造业的名词 industry。词根以 industr- 形式出现。

items.meaningCN: 工业；行业；勤勉（经古法语来自拉丁 industria）
items.example: The car industry is the largest employer in the region.
items.exampleCN: 汽车工业是该地区最大的雇主。

items.meaningCN: 勤劳的；勤勉的（-ous 形容词后缀）
工业的（-al 拉丁形容词后缀）
items.example: Industrial output fell during the recession.
items.exampleCN: 经济衰退期间工业产出下降。

items.meaningCN: 使工业化（-ize 动词后缀）
items.example: The plan aimed to industrialize the interior.
items.exampleCN: 该计划旨在使内陆地区工业化。

items.example: Industrialization brought both wealth and smog.
items.exampleCN: 工业化既带来财富，也带来烟雾。

items.meaningCN: 工业化的（-ed 形容词后缀）
items.example: Industrialized economies usually have a larger service sector.
items.exampleCN: 工业化经济体通常拥有更庞大的服务业。

items.meaning: an owner or manager of large industry
items.example: The industrialist donated land for a school.
items.exampleCN: 这位工业家捐地建了一所学校。

items.meaning: a social order centred on large-scale industry
items.meaningCN: 工业主义（-ism 制度／学说名词）
items.exampleCN: 工业主义重塑了家庭生活。

items.meaning: the decline of manufacturing in a region
items.example: Deindustrialization left empty factories along the canal.
items.exampleCN: 去工业化在运河边留下空置的工厂。

definition_zh: 牛排；肉排；鱼排；碎牛肉（beef steak 口语用法）
definition_en: a thick flat piece of meat or fish cut from an animal and cooked by grilling or frying
core_image: 铁板上一块厚切的肉，边缘滋滋冒起油花
scene: 生日晚上，餐厅铁板端上桌还冒着白烟。 He ordered a medium-rare steak with pepper sauce for his birthday dinner.
sceneCN: 这里 steak 是「牛排」（第 1 个义项：厚切的烤肉块）；句意为他生日晚餐点了一份五分熟牛排配胡椒酱。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加复合成分构成，义为「牛排馆」
由 beef 加本词构成的复合词，义为「牛排；牛排番茄」

senses.title: A thick slice of beef cooked by grilling or frying
senses.definition: a thick flat piece of beef, usually grilled or fried and served whole
senses.definitionCN: 一块厚而平的牛肉，通常整块烤制或煎制后上桌
senses.example: The chef grilled the steak over charcoal for six minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 厨师用炭火把牛排烤了六分钟。
senses.why: One thick slab cut straight from the animal, cooked on its own.
senses.whyCN: 从整块肉上直切下来的厚板，独自受火而成。

senses.title: A thick slice of other meat or fish
senses.definition: a similar thick piece cut from pork, lamb, tuna, salmon, or other flesh
senses.definitionCN: 从猪肉、羊肉、金枪鱼、三文鱼等切下的类似厚块
senses.example: She pan-fried a tuna steak with lemon and herbs.
senses.exampleCN: 她用平底锅煎了一块配柠檬香草的金枪鱼排。
senses.why: The same slab shape, cut from another body.
senses.whyCN: 同样的厚板形状，只是取自另一副躯体。

senses.title: Minced beef used for pies and stews
senses.definition: beef cut into small pieces for slow cooking, as in steak and kidney pie
senses.definitionCN: 切成小块用于慢炖的牛肉，如牛肉腰子派
senses.example: He bought steak for the winter stew at the butcher's.
senses.exampleCN: 他在肉铺买了炖冬季浓汤用的牛肉块。
senses.why: The slab broken down into small squares for the long pot.
senses.whyCN: 厚板被改刀成小块，投入需要久煨的锅里。

intro.en: Steak comes from an Old Norse word for a thick slice roasted on a stick or spit.
intro.cn: steak 源自古诺斯语，指串在签或烤叉上的厚肉片。

items.en: A reconstructed root *staik- meant to stick or pierce, related to pointed objects.
items.cn: 重构词根 *staik- 意为穿刺、签插，与尖物相关。

items.en: Steik meant a thick piece of meat roasted on a spit.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 steik 指串在烤叉上炙烤的厚肉块。

items.en: Steike entered English through northern dialects for a slice of meat for roasting.
items.cn: 中古英语 steike 经北方方言进入英语，指用于烤制的肉片。

items.en: Spelling settled as steak, and the word covered slices of beef chiefly.
items.cn: 拼写定型为 steak，词义以牛肉切片为主。

items.en: The word widened to fish steaks and minced stewing beef, and steakhouse was formed.
items.cn: 词义扩展到鱼排与炖用牛肉块，并衍生出 steakhouse 一词。

note.en: Steak looks like the unrelated stake, and sits near different-root words for cut meat.
note.cn: steak 拼写上与不相关的 stake 相近，义场靠近词源不同的切肉词。

entries.definition: a pointed wooden post, or money risked in a bet
entries.definitionCN: 木桩；赌注；与 steak 只是发音相同，词源不同

entries.definition: a thin branch or a narrow rod
entries.definitionCN: 棍；枝条；拼写相近但词源不同

entries.definition: a neat pile of things placed one on another
entries.definitionCN: 堆；垛；拼写相近但词源不同

entries.definition: a small piece of meat cut with part of the rib bone
entries.definitionCN: 排骨；带骨肉块，切法与部位与牛排不同

entries.definition: a thin slice of meat, often coated and fried
entries.definitionCN: 肉饼；炸肉片，较薄且常裹粉

entries.definition: a boneless piece of meat or fish
entries.definitionCN: 去骨的肉片或鱼片，强调无骨

entries.definition: a large piece of meat cooked whole in an oven
entries.definitionCN: 整烤的大块肉，比牛排大得多

normalIntro.en: Separate steak from stake by meaning, and learn the cut-word field together.
normalIntro.cn: 先区分 steak 与 stake，再把「切肉」词场一起记牢。

normal.en: Steak and stake sound the same: one you eat, one you drive into the ground or bet.
normal.cn: steak 与 stake 同音：一个能吃，一个插地或作赌注。

normal.en: Old Norse steik meant meat roasted on a spit, keeping the stick idea.
normal.cn: 古诺斯语 steik 指烤叉上的肉，保留了「签插」意象。

normal.en: Tuna steak and salmon steak show the fish sense.
normal.cn: tuna steak、salmon steak 展示了鱼排之义。

normal.en: Steak and kidney pie is the famous British stew dish.
normal.cn: steak and kidney pie（牛肉腰子派）是著名的英式炖菜。

normal.en: A steakhouse is a restaurant famous for steak.
normal.cn: steakhouse 是以牛排闻名的餐厅。

abstract.en: Hear the sizzle as a thick slab hits the iron plate.
abstract.cn: 听厚肉块贴上铁板时的滋滋声。

abstract.en: See the smoke rise from a charcoal grill at an open window.
abstract.cn: 看临街窗口炭烤架上腾起的烟。

abstract.en: Picture a knight's spit turning slowly over the fire, meat on a stick.
abstract.cn: 想象骑士时代的烤叉在火上缓缓转动，肉串在签上。

examples.en: She cooks the steak for three minutes on each side.
examples.cn: 她把牛排每面煎三分钟。

examples.en: This restaurant is famous for its grilled steak.
examples.cn: 这家餐厅以烤牛排闻名。

examples.en: A tuna steak needs only a short time in the pan.
examples.cn: 金枪鱼排在锅里只需煎一小会儿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯贴克」——谐音「死贴锅」：牛排死死贴住热锅，滋滋作响。

root: 一般认为源自古诺斯语 steik（烤叉上的厚肉片），词根可上溯至日耳曼语 *staik-（刺、插，与签棒相关）；与同音的 stake（木桩；赌注）词源不同。

sensesIntro.en: From the spit-roasted slab grow slices of beef, thick cuts of other flesh and fish, and the small pieces saved for the stew pot.
sensesIntro.cn: 由叉烤厚板生长出牛排、其他肉与鱼的厚切排，以及留作炖锅的小肉块。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick slab of meat sizzling on iron or spit
core.cn: 核心意象：厚肉块在铁板或烤叉上滋滋作响

branches.en: the classic thick beef cut
branches.cn: 经典的厚切牛排

branches.en: the same slab from fish or other meat
branches.cn: 取自鱼或其他肉的同形厚块

branches.en: small beef squares for the slow pot
branches.cn: 留作慢炖的小牛肉块

branches.en: whole cuts served straight to the plate
branches.cn: 整块切件直接上盘

branches.en: the slab broken down for long cooking
branches.cn: 厚板改刀供久煨

intro.en: Steak is a short root word with few derivatives, joined mainly into eating compounds.
intro.cn: steak 是个短词根词，派生词少，主要参与构成饮食类复合词。

latinIntro.en: Steak has no Latin relatives; it came from Old Norse, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: steak 没有拉丁同源词，源自古诺斯语，故拉丁同族词列表为空。

items.meaning: a thick slice of meat or fish

items.exampleCN: 市中心一家老牌牛排馆

items.meaning: a sharp table knife for cutting steak
a thick slice of beef; also a large tomato type
a pointed post or money risked

makes nouns for a place of business
